description: Storm identifiers of the hurricane loader's twelve catalogue events, read from NOAA NCEI's IBTrACS North Atlantic file by storm name and season. Nothing is synthetic: every row is the archive's own NAME, SEASON and SID for that storm, with the first and last fix time and the number of fixes it holds.
source: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information, International Best Track Archive for Climate Stewardship (IBTrACS) version 4 revision 01, https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/products/international-best-track-archive. US Government work, public domain.
notes: Used by tests/test_loader_defect_fixes.py (TestHurricaneCatalogueIdentifiers). Seven of the catalogue's identifiers (Harvey, Maria, Ian, Michael, Dorian, Ida, Matthew) were not IBTrACS identifiers at all, so those events returned no track; the test holds the catalogue to this file. An identifier is the year, the day of year, and the hemisphere, latitude and longitude of the storm's first fix; IBTrACS does not reissue them, but a later revision of the archive may add fixes to a storm, so the fix counts and times are a record of this reading, not something the test asserts.

catalogue_storm_ids.csv.method: GET by HurricaneLoader._download_ibtracs_csv (file Last-Modified: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 10:11:03 GMT, Content-Length 57593323); rows selected where NAME and SEASON equal the catalogue storm's, one distinct SID per storm; columns NAME, SEASON, SID plus min/max ISO_TIME and the row count. Not verbatim bytes: a twelve-row extract of a 57 MB file.
catalogue_storm_ids.csv.content: Twelve North Atlantic storms: KATRINA 2005, SANDY 2012, MATTHEW 2016, HARVEY, IRMA and MARIA 2017, MICHAEL 2018, DORIAN 2019, IDA 2021, IAN 2022, HELENE and MILTON 2024.
